commits.pr_title: [PCP] Support prefill context parallelism with data parallelism
commits.pr_body:
Enable prefill context parallelism (PCP) with data parallelism (DP), including expert-parallel MoE and MTP decoding.

Reuse existing communication groups, add sequence-parallel GLM MoE support, and fix DP padding and idle-rank handling in PCP draft execution. No new process group.

Continues #54131 with the original authorship preserved; supersedes the earlier approach in #49246.

Validation:

- `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_pcp_dp.py`: 16 passed. Broader focused suite: 170 passed, 10 GPU-only skips.
- `git diff --name-only f2aad6aa70 -z | xargs -0 .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files`: passed.
- GLM-4.7-Flash, MTP3, full decode CUDA graphs: GSM8K 52/64 with EP (TP2×PCP2×DP2), 54/64 without EP (TP1×PCP2×DP2). Both passed all nine uneven-load/idle-rank stress requests. An initial non-EP run had one unparseable answer; it did not reproduce.

ROCm and performance parity remain untested. These GSM8K runs are smoke evaluations.

AI assistance: Claude and Codex.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCM] Add the Fusion E2E TP2 Quick group on MI355, and the AITER MLA fix it needs
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

**Add one AMD CI group.** It mirrors `(H100) Fusion E2E TP2 Quick`, keeping only the payloads the two AITER backends support, and is split out of #50519 so it can be reviewed and validated on its own.

**The test could not run on AMD.** `test_tp2_ar_rms_fp8_fusions` was CUDA only and offered three NVIDIA backends, so the models and backends are now parametrized per platform and `ROCM_AITER_MLA` is added as a backend case.

**The group's third command crashed the worker.** DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite at TP2 gives 8 heads per rank, which selects AITER's Gluon MLA decode on gfx950. Past 2 GiB of KV cache per layer that kernel swaps its masked `buffer_load` for an
unmasked `global_load` and reads outside the allocation:

> Memory access fault by GPU node-4 on address ... Reason: Unknown.

The fault surfaces in whichever kernel runs next, so the traceback points at the Triton MoE rather than at the attention kernel that caused it. Reported upstream as ROCm/aiter#4490, which is open with no reproducer.

### What changed

- Models and attention backends in `test_tp2_ar_rms_fp8_fusions` are chosen per platform. On ROCm the AITER all-reduce 
  pass owns the post-AR RMS sites, so the group checks `aiter_ar_rms_fusion` instead of the native fusions. DeepSeek-Coder
  on AITER MLA runs its MoE on Triton, since AITER's MoE GEMM rejects the reduced dummy shape; Llama-3 gets 
  explicit memory limits to fit alongside the second rank.
- The group is added as a `mirror: amd:` block and as the matching legacy `test-amd.yaml` entry. Three commands, 
   60 minute  budget.
- AITER MLA refuses the Gluon decode once the per-layer cache passes 2 GiB and takes the padded persistent-scheduling 
  ASM decode instead. The bound mirrors the kernel's own `within_2gb` computation, so the fallback engages exactly where the
  unmasked path takes over.
- The builder now derives the per-layer cache size, so the hand-built builder stand-ins in `test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py` 
   gain the two fields it reads, and a new routing test covers the bound.

## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950), two GPUs. The whole group, all three commands in sequence as Buildkite runs it, plus the AITER MLA routing tests the new bound affects.

## Test Result

**Group.** Passes end to end

**Gluon guard.** Above the bound the kernel faults at every KV length tried (1, 64, 128, 129, 256); below it the same shapes are clean. End to end the ASM decode lands within about 2% of Gluon.

**Routing tests.** 552 passed; the new bound test fails when the guard is removed.

---

commits.pr_title: [Test][Determinism] Cover chunked prefill in the batch-invariance suite
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Batch invariance is what stops the same request coming back with different text
depending on how busy the server was. `tests/v1/determinism/` guards that — but
not for chunked prefill, which is what a loaded server does constantly: a long
prompt is split across several scheduler steps, and the later chunks attend over
KV computed in the earlier ones.

The suite says so itself, in a TODO left by #32561:

```python
# TODO: Update prompts to have ragged lengths in order to test chunked prefill
#       The above tests are not currently long enough to exercise chunking.
```

It is accurate. Every prompt in
`test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_bs1_vs_bsN` is short — 356 tokens for
the whole 32-prompt batch against a default budget of 2048 — so a prefill is
never split, and nothing checks that a user gets identical output whether or not
the scheduler chopped their prompt up.

## What this adds

`test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_ragged_chunked_prefill`: a ragged batch
of short, medium and long prompts with the token budget set below the longest
prompt, asserting bitwise-identical logprobs and identical sampled tokens
between bs=1 and bs=N.

I checked against the scheduler that prefills really are split, and that bs=1
and bs=N split the *same* prompt differently — different chunk boundaries, and
sometimes a different number of chunks. That difference is the point: the output
has to stay put regardless.

The budget is derived from the tokenized prompts rather than hardcoded, so the
test cannot quietly stop chunking if `VLLM_TEST_MODEL` changes the tokenizer.
`LLM_with_max_seqs` gains an optional `max_num_batched_tokens` (default `None`).
No non-test code is touched.

## Test Plan

1x RTX 3060 (12 GiB, sm_86), on the default model `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B`:

```bash
VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.5 pytest \
  tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -q -k ragged_chunked_prefill
# 3 passed in 115.52s   (FLASH_ATTN, TRITON_ATTN, FLEX_ATTENTION)
```

Re-run with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0` it fails on every prompt on every backend
(42/42), so it can actually catch a regression. The needle test — the only other
caller of the helper — still passes (6 passed, at reduced settings to fit
12 GiB). `pre-commit run --files ...` is clean.

**SM90 confirmed** — @yuvalluria ran the three parametrisations on an H100 NVL
(Torch 2.13.0+cu130, vLLM 0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b): FLASH_ATTN,
FLEX_ATTENTION and TRITON_ATTN all pass, 3 passed in 208.27s. That covers the
path I could not reach on sm_86, where the Triton matmul overrides and cuBLAS
workspace pinning differ.

The A100/H100/B200 Batch Invariance jobs in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`
run this file with no `-k` filter and list `tests/v1/determinism/` in
`source_file_dependencies`, so CI will exercise it on all three.

Cost is ~2 min for three backends, mostly engine startup, and only in those
dedicated jobs.

## Model evaluation

Not applicable: a test plus an optional keyword argument on a test-local helper.
No model, kernel or serving code changes.

## Not a duplicate

Checked 2026-09-10. No open PR adds chunked-prefill coverage here. #45819
(GDN_ATTN) re-indents this same test function and carries the TODO along
unchanged — happy to rebase if it lands first. #46592 (prefix cache) adds a
canonical prefill chunk size, which this test would then cover.

The new test does share its comparison loop with `bs1_vs_bsN`. That duplication
predates this PR — `bs1_vs_bsN` and `..._should_fail` are already 107 identical
lines out of 128 — and I would rather deduplicate all three in a follow-up than
reshape two existing tests here.

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed every changed line and ran the
tests and linters above on my own hardware.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DSA] Bound DeepSelect sentinel columns in the sparse top-k remap
commits.pr_body:
## Problem and fix

DSV4.1 startup can hit a CUDA illegal memory access in `_sparse_topk_remap_kernel`. Dummy runs feed NaN indexer logits by design (`deep_select_topk` disables its NaN trap for this reason). For a row with NaN inside its valid prefix and `end > topk`, DeepSelect writes an internal sentinel (`0x3f3f3f3f`) to slot 0 of the output row and returns without writing the other slots, which keep whatever the `col_indices` scratch held (the previous call's columns, always in `[0, width)` or `-1`). The remap only rejected negative columns, so slot 0 indexed `sparse_indices[row, 0x3f3f3f3f // SBK]`, about 500 MiB past the row. Whether that faults depends on what happens to be mapped there: it crashes on some layouts (observed on TP4) and silently writes garbage positions on others.

Treat columns outside `[0, width)` as invalid, like `-1`. For a NaN row this makes slot 0 `-1`; the other slots remap stale in-bounds columns, which is harmless for the dummy runs that produce NaN logits. Finite logits are unaffected, since DeepSelect only returns columns below `end <= width`.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  -k "sparse_topk_remap or candidate_blocks_to_sparse or sparse_mqa_logits" -q -rs

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/sparse_mqa_logits.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py
```

- **8 passed**, 7 skipped (need a standalone `deep_gemm`) on GB200. The new test fails on main (slot 0 of NaN rows remaps to garbage) and passes with this change; it zeroes the scratch like the production `col_indices_buffer` so it does not depend on allocator contents.
- Single-GPU repro at production shape (width 16384, topk 512, SBK 8, 128 NaN rows, `expandable_segments`): main raises an illegal memory access; with this change every sentinel slot is `-1`.
- Pre-commit passed.
- No model eval: outputs for finite logits are unchanged.

## Related work and AI assistance

Open-PR search found no equivalent fix. #49897 routes SM12x prefill top-k around a different NaN-broken kernel path and does not touch this remap.

Claude Code assisted with root-causing, implementation and validation; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Share BF16 baselines across quantization comparison tests
commits.pr_body:
## What

`test_fp8_per_channel.py` and `test_mxfp8.py` each boot the model twice: once unquantized to build a BF16 reference, once quantized to compare against it. Both files compute that reference from identical inputs (same model, prompts, `max_model_len`, `max_tokens`, `num_logprobs`), so the second one redoes work the first already did.

This adds a session-scoped `quant_baseline_logprobs` fixture in a new `tests/models/quantization/conftest.py` that computes each reference once per config and caches the outputs.

Only the outputs are cached. Every engine still goes through `VllmRunner.__exit__`, so test isolation is unchanged.

## Timing

Measured on MI300X, `tests/models/quantization/test_fp8_per_channel.py` + `test_mxfp8.py`:

| | Engine boots | Wall time |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 10 | 425.1 s |
| After | 8 | **247.9 s** |

**177 s saved (1.71x).** It removes 2 boots but saves more than that ratio suggests because the deduplicated boots are the `[moe]` baseline (`OLMoE-1B-7B`), where load and memory profiling dominate the group.


## Not a duplicate

The only open PR touching this test group is #56870, which edits `.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml` to split the job into GPTQ Marlin / AWQ / other. That splits the group across runners; this reduces the work inside it. No file overlap, and the two compose.

commits.pr_title: [5/12][ci-selector][CI] Skip the Proton GPU test when another CUPTI tool is injected
commits.pr_body:
Part 5 of the ci-selector series (test selection in [vllm-project/ci-infra](https://github.com/vllm-project/ci-infra)); the other parts are ci-infra PRs.

## Purpose

CI's recording runs, the daily and nightly full runs, load a kernel-launch recorder into every CUDA process through `CUDA_INJECTION64_PATH`. The recorder is a CUPTI injection library. A process gets one CUPTI subscriber, and Proton subscribes itself, so `test_proton_cuda_graph_replay_attribution_on_gpu` fails on every parametrization with:

```
RuntimeError: Failed to execute cuptiSubscribe with error 39
RuntimeError: Failed to execute cuptiActivityFlushAll with error 39
```

This has turned `v1-executor-worker` red on every recording run since the recorder landed: daily 90513, and the fork run 90641. The same step passes on main without the recorder, including 90628 at 90641's commit.

This PR skips exactly that test when `CUDA_INJECTION64_PATH` is set. Everywhere else it runs as before, and the step's other 806 tests keep recording. The Proton tests that mock the profiler are unaffected.

## Test Plan

Run `v1-executor-worker` from this branch with the kernel recorder on: `VLLM_CI_KERNREC=1`, `VLLM_CI_ONLY_STEP_KEYS=["v1-executor-worker"]`, [vllm/ci #90780](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90780).

## Test Result

`v1-executor-worker` passed with the recorder loaded (`kernrec: on` in the log): **817 passed, 5 skipped**. The four Proton parametrizations were the skips:

```
test_proton_cuda_graph_replay_attribution_on_gpu[hatchet-shadow] SKIPPED (Another CUPTI tool is injected (CUDA_INJEC...)
test_proton_cuda_graph_replay_attribution_on_gpu[hatchet-python] SKIPPED (...)
test_proton_cuda_graph_replay_attribution_on_gpu[hatchet_msgpack-shadow] SKIPPED (...)
test_proton_cuda_graph_replay_attribution_on_gpu[hatchet_msgpack-python] SKIPPED (...)
```

Before this change, the same step with the recorder failed exactly these four: 4 failed, 806 passed, on daily 90513 and on 90641. Without the recorder, `CUDA_INJECTION64_PATH` is unset and the test runs as before.

## Purpose

Disable JIT kernel warmup by default in the test-only `VllmRunner` fixture. Tests can retain production behavior by passing `kernel_config={"enable_jit_warmup": True}` explicitly. Server helpers and the vLLM product default are unchanged.

In [(H200 MIG 35GB) Quantized Models build 90696](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90696#01a0ceea-8e6b-451c-8f44-64de37cdbdd8), the 13 non-eager engine starts spent 933.31 seconds in JIT kernel warmup out of a 3245.48-second job. Most of those tests use only a small subset of the 121 compiled sampler keys.

This is not a duplicate of #58197 or #55146. Those PRs connect eager mode and MRV2 to the existing warmup flag; this PR changes only the default used by the offline test fixture.

AI assistance was used to analyze the CI log and prepare this change. The submitter reviewed the final diff.

## Test Plan

commits.pr_title: [CI][Bugfix] Limit MRV2 sampler JIT warmup registration to ROCm
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

#58092 ("[ROCm][Bugfix] Register MRV2 sampler JIT warmups") calls `register_top_k_top_p_warmups()` in the MRV2 `GPUModelRunner` on **all** platforms, not just ROCm. On CUDA these Triton sampler warmups recompile on most engine starts (about 110s each, against `finished in 0.00s` before), so NVIDIA CI jobs slowed down a lot and many now time out.

This PR keeps the registration for ROCm, which #58092 targeted, and puts CUDA back where it was before #58092.

## Impact of #58092 on `main` CI

Median passing runtime per step, ~26 `main` builds before vs ~26 after `96e203b08e`:

| Hardware | Steps | ≥15% and ≥3 min slower | faster |
|---|---|---|---|
| NVIDIA | 185 | **46** (+4 that now only time out) | 1 |
| AMD | 175 | 3 (noise) | 0 |

- About **+430 job-minutes per `main` build** on the affected NVIDIA steps.
- **45 timeouts** on 7 steps that never timed out before, e.g. Language Models (Hybrid) Shard 2 ×15 and Basic Correctness ×11.
- Examples: Basic Correctness 42 → 68+ min, PyTorch Compilation 25 → 49, PyTorch Fullgraph 55 → 83, Samplers 23 → 39, H100 Fusion E2E Quick 7 → 15.
- Clean break on `main`: build 90618 (`26879f3260`) ran Basic Correctness in 42 min; the next build, 90619 (`96e203b08e`), took 63 min, and every build since has taken 66–68 min or timed out.
- Per-test view (Basic Correctness, same runner type): every test became about 140s slower, e.g. 43s → 191s, with the time spent in `JIT kernel warmup (120 compile keys)`.

The CUDA `No Runtime JITs E2E` step passed before #58092 without this registration, so leaving it out on CUDA shouldn't bring back runtime JITs there. If CUDA does need these warmups for its FlashInfer fallback, that can come back once the per-start recompile is fixed.

This PR is also why the open timeout bumps (#58376, #58386, #58320) shouldn't be needed.

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `58092`, "Revert 58092", "topk topp warmup", "JIT warmup timeout" and "sampler warmup CUDA". None addresses this; #58410 adds another MRV2 sampler warmup and doesn't touch the platform scope.

## Test Plan

- `ruff check`, `ruff format` and the full pre-commit hook set pass.
- CI: `:amd: (MI355) MRV2 Sampler JIT Warmup` should still pass on ROCm, and NVIDIA steps such as Basic Correctness, PyTorch Compilation and `No Runtime JITs E2E` should go back to their pre-#58092 runtimes.
- No model eval: this changes which kernels are warmed up at startup, not model outputs.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the CI analysis and the change; I reviewed the diff.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix TileLang mHC fused RMSNorm on 64-wide wavefronts
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

27 tests in `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py` fail in the `(MI355) Miscellaneous Kernels` job added by #50519, all with the fused RMSNorm enabled:

```text
FAILED test_mhc_pre_tilelang[True-*] (8 cases)
FAILED test_deepseek_v41_mhc_pre_delayed[True-False-*] (15 cases)
FAILED test_deepseek_v41_decoder_mixes_match_torch[disabled-*] (4 cases)
```

Failing run: <https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13378/list?sid=01a0c82f-6637-4452-80c8-a00e9f20a69b&tab=output>

The fused-norm mHC pre kernels split 96 threads: the mix phase runs on threads 0-31, and the collapse + RMSNorm on threads 32-95. TileLang's HIP AllReduce shuffle phase ignores the thread offset of the reduction group, so on a 64-wide wavefront the RMSNorm reduction sums only half of the values. As a result, layer_input is sqrt(2) times too large. CUDA is not affected because its 32-wide warps keep the group aligned.

On ROCm, the mix phase now runs on the last 32 threads, so the RMSNorm reduction uses threads 0-63, one full wavefront. On CUDA the generated kernel is unchanged.
## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950):

```bash
cd tests
pytest -v kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py kernels/test_mhc_jit_warmup.py kernels/test_mhc_tilelang_jit.py
```

## Test Result

Before:

```text
27 failed, 154 passed, 150 skipped
```

After:

```text
181 passed, 150 skipped
```

AI assistance was used for diagnosis, implementation and validation. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

The existing FusedMoE layer suite had no graph replay coverage for the MoRI path. The MI355 parity audit added a bounded two-GPU contract that changes inputs and routing between replays and checks output lifetime.

The inline TODO keeps that missing work visible. This association does not establish fault-tolerance parity or cover the B200 FusedMoE group’s additional `test_deepep_v2_moe.py` matrix.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Pick a KV block size supported by every attention backend
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #48286.

`Platform.update_block_size_for_backend()` picks the KV cache block size from the **first** non-SSM attention backend only. Models that mix attention backends with disjoint block-size support break: GLM-DSA / DeepSeek-V3.2-style models pair a sparse-MLA main backend (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, supports `[32, 64]`, prefers 32) with `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` (supports only `[64]`). The auto-selected 32 then fails much later in `select_common_block_size()` with the opaque

```
ValueError: No common block size for 32.
```

and the only workaround is a manual `--block-size 64` (undocumented, as #48286 notes).

This PR was split in two to keep the diff reviewable. It now carries backend collection and block-size selection only (+131/-21). Aligning phases 2 and 3 to the full backend list follows in a separate PR once this one merges.

## Changes

- `Platform._find_non_ssm_backend()` becomes `_find_non_ssm_backends()` and returns every distinct non-SSM backend in layer order rather than the first. Both call sites are updated (`interface.py`, `cpu.py`); no caller of the old name remains.
- New `Platform._preferred_block_size_for_backends()` returns the smallest block size every backend accepts:
  - a single backend keeps today's behaviour via `get_preferred_block_size()`;
  - if every backend accepts the default, the default wins;
  - otherwise candidates are the least common multiples formed by taking one supported size per backend, tried in ascending order, and **each candidate is confirmed against every backend** via `supports_block_size()`;
  - if nothing is common it raises `ValueError` naming each backend and its supported sizes.
- Candidates are validated rather than inferred. A backend may override `supports_block_size()` to accept exact sizes only, as CPU_MLA does by accepting 16 but no multiple of it, so "a multiple of a supported size" is not a safe assumption. This is the correctness point @yewentao256 raised in review.
- Phase 1 of `update_block_size_for_backend()` uses the new selection, and the log line now names all participating backends.
- Phases 2 and 3 are unchanged here and still take the first backend, exactly as before this PR.

## Test Plan

New unit tests in `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py`, built on a `_mock_backend` helper that can emulate an exact-size backend:

- `test_preferred_block_size_satisfies_every_backend`, parametrized:
  - a lone `MultipleOf(8)` backend keeps the default 16;
  - `[32, 64]` plus `[64]` gives 64, the #48286 shape;
  - `[32, 64]` alone still gives 32;
  - `[32]` plus `[48]` gives 96.
- `test_preferred_block_size_searches_past_an_exact_size_backend`: an exact-size backend accepting `[16, 96]` beside `MultipleOf(32)` gives 96, where a greedy lcm(16, 32) = 32 would be wrongly accepted.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Select one GPU for the H200 initialized snapshot E2E step
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`:nvidia: (H200) Initialized Snapshot E2E` (added in #51360) fails on the `H200` queue with:

```
initialized snapshot E2E: the runner must expose exactly one selected GPU
```

The step uses `no_plugin: true`, so the script runs on the host and picks its GPU from `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, or a single `nvidia.com/gpu=<id>` CDI device. On `H200` queue hosts, one agent owns the whole machine and none of these name a single GPU. The CDI hook resolves to `nvidia.com/gpu=all`, which the script correctly rejects.

This pins `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: "0"` in the step env. The script resolves index 0 to its UUID, checks that it is a full non-MIG H200, and passes only that device to its container (`--gpus device=<uuid>`). Because the value is step-scoped, the other H200 steps, which propagate their environment into multi-GPU containers, are unaffected.

## Test Plan

A scoped Buildkite build (`VLLM_CI_ONLY_STEP_KEYS=["initialized-snapshot-e2e"]`) on this branch.

Pending, linked below once complete.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Use breakable CUDA graphs (no torch.compile) by default under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT so the tuned matmul configs see the runtime M
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` routes every linear layer through the batch-invariant persistent Triton matmul, which picks its tile config from a per-architecture table keyed by `(N, K)` and an **M bucket** (#53247 Ada/Hopper, #53649 SM100, #57456 SM120). On the default `torch.compile` path that lookup (`_get_matmul_config`, called from `matmul_persistent`) runs while Dynamo traces the model with the compile-time dummy M, and the selected `BLOCK_M / BLOCK_N / num_warps / num_stages` are frozen in the graph. Every decode step therefore runs with the largest bucket's configs (#54243): on RTX PRO 6000 that is 3-6x slower per GEMM than the `M <= 8` configs the tables were tuned for, and it is where essentially all of the remaining batch-invariance overhead goes ([profile](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54243#issuecomment-5723774275)).

Without `torch.compile` the lookup executes at CUDA graph capture time with each capture size's real M, and the tables work as intended. This PR makes batch-invariant mode default to that path via the existing breakable CUDA graph mechanism (#42304, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`), following the same opt-in pattern as `default_breakable_cudagraph_architectures`. It is in line with moving models off `torch.compile` (as suggested in #54503) and needs no change to the matmul or the tables.

## Changes

- `vllm/config/vllm.py`: `_maybe_enable_breakable_cudagraph` also auto-enables breakable CUDA graphs when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the platform is CUDA, the model is bf16 and unquantized, `enforce_eager` is off, sequence parallelism / async TP were not explicitly enabled (they are `torch.compile` passes), and at least one of the per-rank `(N, K)` shapes of the linear layers inside the compiled forward (qkv_proj / o_proj / gate_up_proj / down_proj, derived from `ModelConfig` + TP size; `lm_head` runs in `compute_logits()` outside the compiled graph and does not count) is a key of the device's tuned table. Only when the user did not set `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` themselves; `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` opts out (old behaviour). Logged once.
- `tests/test_config.py`: one parametrized config-level test (`test_batch_invariant_breakable_cudagraph`, 11 cases: on; BI off; explicit opt-out; eager; SP enabled; fp16; quantized; untuned shapes; TP=4 per-rank hit; list-valued `intermediate_size`; no table).
- `docs/features/batch_invariance.md`: one item under "Implementation Details".

No change for `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0`, ROCm/XPU, devices without a tuned table, or models whose shapes / dtype the table does not cover (those keep `torch.compile`, since `_get_matmul_config` would fall back to the default config anyway).

## Test Plan

Hardware: one node with RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120, 96 GB, PCIe), driver 580.159.04; torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1; `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`. The latency numbers below were taken with this PR's first commit on main @ dbf4b89cf2 and the gsm8k numbers (in the comments) at 05fba88af; both trees carried the sm_120 table from #57456, which has since been merged. The gate changes in later commits do not alter the runtime path for these models (their qkv / gate_up / down shapes are in the table), and the final head was re-checked on the same GPU (unit tests + Qwen3-1.7B decode: 0.524 s auto-enabled vs 1.480 s with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`).

Same protocol as #53649 / #57456, all runs in one job on the same GPU per model:

```bash
# BI=1, this PR (breakable CUDA graphs auto-enabled)
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --num-iters-warmup 3 --num-iters 10                                   # decode-heavy (defaults: input 32 / output 128 / batch 8)
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --num-iters-warmup 3 --num-iters 10 --input-len 1024 --output-len 32 --batch-size 8   # prefill-heavy
# BI=1, opt-out on this PR (== previous behaviour, torch.compile path)
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --num-iters-warmup 3 --num-iters 10
# BI=1 on main (same commands, main checkout) and BI=0 reference
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0 vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --num-iters-warmup 3 --num-iters 10
```
Same for `Qwen/Qwen3-4B`, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, plus `-tp 2` on Qwen3-8B.

Correctness / invariance on this PR:

```bash
pytest -q tests/test_config.py -k breakable
pytest -q tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py
pytest -q tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k "bs1_vs_bsN and (FLASH_ATTN or TRITON_ATTN)"
VLLM_NEEDLE_TRIALS=3 VLLM_NEEDLE_BATCH_SIZE=64 pytest -q tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k "needle and FLASH_ATTN"
```

## Test Result

All numbers from one job, one GPU per model, `vllm bench latency --num-iters-warmup 3 --num-iters 10`, avg latency in seconds. "main" = main @ dbf4b89cf2 (+ #57456's table); "this PR, opt-out" = this PR with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`, i.e. the previous behaviour on the same tree. Every "this PR" run logged `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1: auto-enabling VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 ...` and ran with `CompilationMode.NONE`; every other run ran with `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`.

**Decode-heavy (input 32 / output 128 / batch 8)**

| model | BI=0 | BI=1 main | BI=1 this PR, opt-out | BI=1 this PR | change vs main | BI overhead main -> this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-1.7B | 0.4849 | 1.4305 | 1.4303 | **0.5211** | -63.6% | 2.95x -> 1.07x |
| Qwen3-4B | 0.9366 | 2.3578 | 2.3159 | **0.9797** | -58.4% | 2.52x -> 1.05x |
| Qwen3-8B | 1.5175 | 3.4567 | 3.4408 | **1.5818** | -54.2% | 2.28x -> 1.04x |

**Prefill-heavy (input 1024 / output 32 / batch 8)**

| model | BI=0 | BI=1 main | BI=1 this PR, opt-out | BI=1 this PR | change vs main | BI overhead main -> this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-1.7B | 0.2236 | 0.4674 | 0.4692 | **0.2590** | -44.6% | 2.09x -> 1.16x |
| Qwen3-4B | 0.4530 | 0.8095 | 0.8098 | **0.5024** | -37.9% | 1.79x -> 1.11x |
| Qwen3-8B | 0.7928 | 1.2641 | 1.2640 | **0.8254** | -34.7% | 1.59x -> 1.04x |

**TP=2, Qwen3-8B, decode-heavy, BI=1:** main 2.9336 s, this PR opt-out 2.9958 s, this PR 2.8955 s (-1.3%). No gain is expected here because the sm_120 table only has the TP=1 shapes (per-rank shapes fall back to the default config), and there is no regression.

The remaining 4-16% over BI=0 is the batch-invariant kernels themselves plus the Inductor fusions given up by not compiling (with BI=0 the same breakable path costs 2-6% on these workloads, measured in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54243#issuecomment-5723774275). Kernel-level, the persistent matmul is at cuBLAS parity for decode on this path (370 ms vs 388 ms of GEMM time over 128 decode steps of Qwen3-1.7B, vs 1349 ms with the frozen bucket; same comment).

Tests on this PR (+ #57456's table), same GPU type:

```
$ pytest -q tests/test_config.py -k breakable
29 passed, 367 deselected, 14 warnings in 9.11s
$ pytest -q tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py
34 passed, 14 warnings in 13.30s
$ pytest -q tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k "bs1_vs_bsN and (FLASH_ATTN or TRITON_ATTN)"
4 passed, 15 deselected, 14 warnings in 126.36s (0:02:06)
$ VLLM_NEEDLE_TRIALS=3 VLLM_NEEDLE_BATCH_SIZE=64 pytest -q tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k "needle and FLASH_ATTN"
2 passed, 17 deselected, 14 warnings in 44.28s
```

The generation tests above run the auto-enabled path (re-running the `bs1_vs_bsN and TRITON_ATTN` pair with `pytest -s` shows the auto-enable log line and both engines starting with `CompilationMode.NONE` / `Breakable CUDA graph enabled`).

Plus a TP=2 bitwise check on this PR (Qwen3-1.7B, 64 prompts x 24 greedy tokens, sampled-token logprobs compared bitwise: single-request vs batched and repeat vs repeat, prefix caching off): 0 / 1536 mismatches in all four comparisons, with the auto-enable log line present.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix startup OOM in AITER MLA FP8 prefill workspace sizing
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes a startup OOM on Kimi K2.5 (or similar) when using the AITER ASM MLA prefill kernel, caused by overly pessimistic bounds on the size of the required persistent metadata buffers. These sizes were subsequently passed to the workspace manager which triggered the OOM.

**Triggered by**: The AITER bump to v0.1.22post1 picked up ROCm/aiter#3606 which slightly changed the logic for workspace sizing. 

**Long term fix in AITER**: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5759

### Why

For causal FP8 MLA the AITER backend uses a persistent kernel. It needs buffers to hold the work items to be completed by each work group. The metadata scheduler is responsible for sizing these buffers so that they are sufficiently large to handle any requests that might come in.  

The MLA metadata scheduler now emits a very loose bound. The bound is based on the assumption that every request can use max_qlen query tokens. (The actual upper bound is that the sum of query tokens equals max_num_batched_tokens). If one uses these to size the logits/attn_lse partial buffers we get huge KV reservations:

| max_num_batched_tokens | before aiter#3606 | after aiter#3606 (OOM) | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8192  | 1.88 GiB | 64.03 GiB  | 2.56 GiB |
| 16384 | 3.75 GiB | 128.03 GiB | 2.62 GiB |

**Short term fix**: Size with assumption that the total query tokens is bounded by the token budget.

**Long term fix**: AITER should give us this budget-aware max buffer size. Ticket: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/5729

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Restore successful push completion reporting
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

After #56104, successful NIXL push WRITEs are filtered through `_recving_metadata`, which tracks incoming requests. Ordinary producer requests have no entry there, so they never report `finished_sending` after their WRITEs complete and retain source KV blocks until lease expiry. The existing test injects a consumer acknowledgment that the push implementation does not send.

Report successful outgoing requests when every WRITE handle has been released. Track outbound submission and polling failures across polls so a later successful sibling cannot hide an earlier failure. Ignore late completions for requests already retired by lease expiry, avoiding duplicate scheduler completion reports.

Regression coverage includes staggered successful WRITEs (including PP/HMA), sibling failures, submission/release failures, and completion after expiry. The preexisting lease-expiry behavior while DMA remains active is outside this change.

Duplicate-work check: searched open PRs referencing #56104 and NIXL push completion/failure, and inspected the related changes. #50754 adds decode-side notification of failed WRITE submissions; #55470 prevents deferred WRITEs after producer retirement. Neither restores producer completion reporting for successful WRITEs or tracks outgoing failures across completion polls. This follows up the already-merged #56104.

## Test Plan

Run the existing push unit suite with mocked NIXL transfers. On the local macOS environment, apply the existing `skip_global_cleanup` marker to avoid an unrelated PyTorch MPS allocator assertion during teardown. No test bodies are skipped. The existing virtualenv interpreter was used (shown below as `.venv/bin/python`):

```bash
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import pytest
class CpuOnlyTests:
    def pytest_collection_modifyitems(self, items):
        for item in items:
            item.add_marker(pytest.mark.skip_global_cleanup)
raise SystemExit(pytest.main(
    ['tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py', '-q'],
    plugins=[CpuOnlyTests()],
))
PY

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/push_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
git diff --cached --check
```

## Test Result

- Push unit suite on base `ca831d1c55` plus this change: **84 passed**.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks and whitespace checks passed.
- Independent AI review checked the changed lifecycle paths; its expiry/late-completion finding was fixed and covered by tests.
- GPU/NIXL serving tests and model evaluations have not been run. These unit tests do not establish real RDMA behavior or performance.

## AI assistance / draft status

AI assistance (Codex) was used to implement, test, and review this change. The tests above were run by the assistant. This PR remains a draft pending the human submitter's line-by-line review, independent test execution, and serving/model validation required by the contribution policy.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Validate Mooncake and NIXL prefill/decode accuracy
commits.pr_body:
- Add two Mooncake HIP and six NIXL/AITER cases, preserving upstream model/TP pairs, all 1,319 GSM8K questions, 100 concurrent requests and the original accuracy bounds.
- Pin model/tokenizer revisions and require positive evaluation-only external-KV deltas; also require transferred bytes for NIXL, with explicit cache bounds and owned-process cleanup.
- Add MI355 native mirrors and matching optional legacy jobs, preserving the existing NVIDIA and generic Triton NIXL selections.

The existing AMD generic NIXL sweep already covers these model and tensor-parallel combinations with Triton attention. The missing upstream counterparts exercise a second attention backend and Mooncake transfer, so these tests use AITER unified attention and native Mooncake HIP transport. Reusing the original accuracy functions preserves their full workload and acceptance bounds. Evaluation-only counters establish that transferred KV contributes during GSM8K beyond the preliminary smoke request.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and validation.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Extend QK-norm/RoPE/KV-cache fusion to MRoPE
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Extend the existing `QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass` to support Qwen3-VL 3D MRoPE. For eligible decode ranges, it replaces two Q/K RMSNorm launches, MRoPE, and the unified FP8 KV-cache update with one AITER attention-prologue kernel: **three fewer GPU launches per layer**.

This is a model-agnostic compile-pass integration: it removes the earlier Qwen3-specific flag/wrapper and uses the existing O2/O3 pass controls. Unsupported configurations stay on the unfused path.

![Before and after GPU trace: separate operations fused into one AITER kernel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vorapolsiloai/vllm/93e5d01e7e12610a3ae8371801aae2036342ff16/pr-assets/vllm-50212-before-after.png)

## Review guide

1. `matcher_utils.py` and `qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py`: match 3D MRoPE and emit the fused replacement.
2. `_aiter_ops.py`, `attention/backend.py`, and `rocm_aiter_unified_attn.py`: capability gate and backend-owned kernel dispatch/cache handling.
3. `rotary_embedding/mrope.py`: expose MRoPE as a matchable custom op on HIP only.
4. `attention.py`: keep scalar Quark query scales per-tensor unless per-head scaling is explicitly enabled. This fixes TP4/TP8 when one KV head is local to each rank.
5. `test_rocm_aiter_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py`: correctness, rejection, layout, version-gate, and TP regressions.

## Safety and compatibility

- Only ROCm AITER unified decoder attention opts in; other backends reject by default.
- CUDA/XPU MRoPE behavior is unchanged.
- Fusion is rejected for observable rotated K, unsupported dimensions/layouts, unsupported AITER builds, and ranges above the existing 256-token limit.
- Full/partial rotary, NeoX/GPT-J pairing, interleaved/non-interleaved MRoPE, and LBHNC/LBNHC/LHBNC cache layouts are covered.
- Opaque `LayerName` patterns are registered once on torch >= 2.11 to avoid duplicate wildcard patterns.

### AITER requirement

Requires a build containing the strided KV-cache fix from [AITER #4531](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4531) ([`b0cc5392`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/b0cc5392dd838a4bec46a5553e7fbeed60218ab5)); the first containing tag is [`v0.1.20.dev1`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/tree/v0.1.20.dev1). Builds known not to contain it (`v0.1.20.dev0`, `v0.1.20`, and `v0.1.20.post1`) cleanly fall back to the unfused path.

## Validation

- Full ROCm compile-pass sweep: **1,020 passed** with the AITER #4531 source.
- Final scalar-query-scale regression: **3/3 passed** for TP2 `(32, 2)`, TP4 `(16, 1)`, and TP8 `(8, 1)` local `(Q heads, KV heads)`.
- Real serving compilation fused all expected layers: **48** for Qwen3-VL-30B TP1 and **94 per rank** for Qwen3-VL-235B TP2/TP4.
- Steady-state Kineto traces confirm one fused call per eligible layer and a net reduction of three launches. Large-prefill ranges remain unfused as intended.
- Ruff, Python compilation, and `git diff --check` passed.

## Performance

MI355X (`gfx950`), 8,192 input / 1,024 output tokens, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, paired fusion OFF/ON runs:

| Model | TP | MC | Output tok/s OFF | Output tok/s ON | Throughput | Mean TPOT OFF -> ON | TPOT |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Qwen3-VL-30B FP8 | 1 | 4 | 538.78 | 623.68 | **+15.76%** | 7.16 -> 6.15 ms | **-14.22%** |
| Qwen3-VL-30B FP8 | 1 | 64 | 2,660.65 | 2,786.82 | **+4.74%** | 22.11 -> 21.06 ms | **-4.72%** |
| Qwen3-VL-30B FP8 | 1 | 256 | 3,556.08 | 3,580.08 | **+0.67%** | 64.58 -> 64.08 ms | **-0.78%** |
| Qwen3-VL-235B MXFP4 | 2 | 4 | 274.39 | 304.65 | **+11.03%** | 13.42 -> 11.99 ms | **-10.66%** |
| Qwen3-VL-235B MXFP4 | 2 | 64 | 1,344.76 | 1,366.77 | **+1.64%** | 43.51 -> 42.82 ms | **-1.59%** |
| Qwen3-VL-235B MXFP4 | 2 | 256 | 1,981.63 | 1,992.43 | **+0.54%** | 113.88 -> 112.99 ms | **-0.78%** |
| Qwen3-VL-235B MXFP4 | 4 | 4 | 306.59 | 341.66 | **+11.44%** | 11.93 -> 10.59 ms | **-11.25%** |
| Qwen3-VL-235B MXFP4 | 4 | 64 | 1,888.43 | 1,985.68 | **+5.15%** | 30.58 -> 29.14 ms | **-4.74%** |
| Qwen3-VL-235B MXFP4 | 4 | 256 | 3,087.00 | 3,132.56 | **+1.48%** | 72.50 -> 71.33 ms | **-1.61%** |

All nine measured point estimates improve. The small high-concurrency deltas require repeated runs before claiming statistical significance. TP8 has targeted correctness coverage but was not rerun end-to-end because the eighth GPU was unavailable.
